items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And very few people could play, aside from Joseph Hoffman and then Rachmaninoff.

ctx.x: I can do it, so I’m going to write it.
Exactly. And very few people could play, aside from Joseph Hoffman and then Rachmaninoff. Because that was a great tradition.

Well, you have to go back to work soon, but I wanted to follow up quickly on one little thing — you mentioned the thing about The Beatles in ‘64. They certainly changed our society but no one ever said anything about the fact that they opened up a market even for jazz musicians to go over?
